chunks: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who performs salat (prayer) in a shift and a khimār, and he said: “There should be upon her a wrap which she gathers around herself.”

What is meant by mentioning the wrap in addition to the shift and the khimār is an increase in merit and reward. It is also possible that what is meant is the case when the shift and the khimār do not cover anything, for whenever the situation is like this, a covering is indispensable.
That which indicates what we have said is what he narrated: and that which al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

key_terms.دِرْعٍ: a shift or long garment worn by a woman
key_terms.سَاتِرٍ: a covering that conceals the body
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةٌ: a wrap or outer covering gathered around the body
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةِ: the woman whose prayer clothing is being discussed

ai.seo_question: What clothing must a woman wear for salat (prayer) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the clothing of a woman in salat (prayer), stating that she should have a wrap over her shift and khimār. The accompanying explanation indicates either that this adds excellence and reward, or that it becomes necessary when the existing garments do not provide adequate covering.
